Hi Taylor / Alicia,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through the primary use cases (provider note summarization + clinical QA). Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can kick off a short qualification pilot: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary success metric: grounding precision on clinical Q&A (min 90% attribution precision on our validation set).
- Latency requirement: 95th percentile < 700ms for single-turn queries at the expected pilot concurrency (10 qps burst 30 qps).
- Data sensitivity: PHI in attachments; you prefer VPC/private deployment or a dedicated instance.

Redwood recommended stack for the pilot (shortlist)
1) Retriever: dense embedding index (FAISS, IVF-PQ) with chunk size 800–1200 tokens and metadata filtering by encounter_id/date.
2) Reranker: cross-encoder reranker (MiniLM-cross or lexical-cross tuned on clinical Q&A) for top-100 -> top-5 refinement.
3) Generator (model candidates): redwood/rei-13b-instruct-qd (quantized 8-bit) for cost/latency balance; fallback to mistral-7b-instruct for low-latency reads.
4) Grounding controls: prefix templates + explicit citation tokens; plan to measure hallucination rate and attribution precision @1/5.

Deliverables we propose for the pilot
- Baseline eval run (your 300 sample queries + our eval prompt set) using three retriever/reranker variants.
- Artifact: per-query attribution table, hallucination flags, latency and token cost breakdown.
- Timeline: baseline run in 7 business days once MedSyn shares the sample set and permission for a short GDPR/PHI dataflow check.

Attachments I’ve included: medsyn_rag-probe.xlsx (sample mapping sheet), eval_prompt_set_v3.jsonl (example prompts), redwood_proposal_medsyn.pdf (commercial + runbook).

Requested actions from MedSyn
1) Share 300 de-identified sample queries + 10 representative long documents (PDFs) — ideally by EOD Wednesday 5/19.
2) Confirm whether you want a Dedicated instance (reserved GPUs) or Private VPC deployment.
3) Procurement contact for initial SOW & timeline.

Next meeting: propose a 30-minute sync on Monday 5/17 to confirm sample set and deployment choice — is 9am PT okay?

Thanks,
Logan

Taylor — great questions. Answering inline and adding next steps. (Forwarding to Karthik and Vanessa for technical/ops details.)

> For the retriever, we currently use a hosted vector DB (vendor-managed). Would Redwood run the FAISS index inside a Dedicated instance, or do you recommend we export to your infra for the pilot?
We can support both flows. For speed of iteration I recommend a short-term export to a Dedicated instance we provision (no long-term vendor lock-in). That lets us run identical FAISS IVF-PQ configs and produce apples-to-apples benchmarks. If you prefer we can also configure a remote connector to your hosted DB, but that adds network variance to latency measurements.

> On reranker: can you quantify the expected latency delta for adding a cross-encoder step (top-100 -> top-5)?
Rough ballpark based on prior clinical pilots:
- Retrieval (embedding + ANN search top-100): ~50–120ms (single-node Dedicated).
- Cross-encoder rerank (top-100): ~200–450ms depending on model size; tuned MiniLM-cross is ~220ms median for top-100 on our infra.
- Generator (redwood/rei-13b-instruct-qd) generation tail + decoding: ~200–400ms for 150 tokens with quantized execution.
Combined 95p: typically 500–850ms. To meet 700ms SLO we recommend one of: reduce reranker top-K to 40, use a smaller cross-encoder for rerank, or use hybrid approach (first bi-encoder coarse rerank -> small cross-encoder top-40). We’ll include these permutations in the baseline run.

> On models: can you send a short benchmark (latency/cost) for the two suggested generators using our target prompt lengths (~600 tokens context, 150 tokens generation)?
Yes — Karthik will attach a compact benchmark table to this thread. Vanessa: attaching the quick bench and the config we typically run for clinical QA (index params, chunk sizing, reranker choice).

Operational notes / data transfer checklist
- Redwood DSA & encryption-in-transit: we use TLS1.3 for all ingests; S3 presigned uploads or secure SFTP are available.
- For PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private VPC; we’ll raise the SOC2 + logging SOPs in the SOW.

Next steps
1) MedSyn to confirm Dedicated vs Private by EOD 5/17.
2) MedSyn to share de-identified sample set and access path by 5/19.
3) Redwood to run baseline matrix (3 retriever/reranker/model combos) and deliver report within 7 business days of data receipt.

Thanks — Karthik / Vanessa, over to you for the bench and the more detailed retrieval config.

—Logan
